title: The Hollow Sigil
premise: Oscar Winterbourne, a scribe bound by debt to the temple of a valley where magic cannot enter, is pressed into flight when a dying stranger leaves them a map inked in blood and a sigil that burns itself into their skin. The map leads to the capital, where King Aldric has been hollowed out and replaced by the Vessel—a crown-born parasite feeding on his memories while wearing his face. As Oscar's borrowed sigil grants them glimpses of the king's stolen past, they realize the stranger was the last royal archivist, and Oscar's own forgotten childhood is tangled in the palace's oldest crime. In the thirteenth moon's eclipse, Oscar must choose between restoring the true king and destroying the sigil-magic entirely, ending with Aldric freed but mortal, the valley's protection broken, and Oscar—no longer debt-bound, no longer invisible—walking out of the valley for good.
about_author: August Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paper, power, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: Ink That Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishes the debt-bound life: copying prayers in a valley where magic dies at the border stones. A bleeding stranger collapses at the scriptorium door, presses a folded map into Oscar's hands, and whispers 'thirteen turns' before dying. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread—the temple elders want the map burned, and Oscar, against all instinct, hides it instead.

chapters.title: The Sigil on My Skin
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The map proves impossible to destroy; overnight its mark transfers to Oscar's wrist as a burning sigil. When temple enforcers come searching, Oscar flees across the border stones—and feels magic touch them for the first time, sickening and vast. Emotional beat: terror mixed with a shameful thrill of freedom as the valley's safety falls away behind them.

chapters.title: Road of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, meeting caravan cook Maren. Traveling under false names toward the capital, Oscar learns the sigil lets them read any written thing—including a wanted notice describing their own face. Maren shares rumors of a king who hasn't spoken aloud in two years. Emotional beat: wary companionship; Oscar begins wanting a life beyond survival.

chapters.title: The City That Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The capital celebrates a king whose edicts contradict each other week to week. Using scribe credentials, Oscar enters the royal archive and finds records altered mid-page—in the same hand, dated years apart. Emotional beat: uncanny horror deepening into resolve; the corruption isn't just of the king but of memory itself.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Oscar infiltrating the palace; interludes from inside King Aldric's fractured mind, where he watches the Vessel wear him like a glove. Oscar witnesses the Vessel feed on a courtier's memories. Emotional beat: pity crystallizing into purpose—Aldric is not dead, only buried.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Decoding the map fully, Oscar finds the dead stranger's hidden letters: the Vessel was bound by the first royal archivists, and the binding requires a bloodline the archives claim ended—yet the letters name a child smuggled to a valley where magic cannot follow. Oscar realizes the child was them. Emotional beat: identity shattered and reassembled; grief for a stolen childhood.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With three nights until the eclipse completes the Vessel's permanent binding, Oscar allies with Maren and a disgraced palace guard. The Vessel, sensing the sigil, sets traps through the city using people's own recorded memories against them. Emotional beat: rising desperation; every ally becomes a liability.

chapters.title: The Price of the Page
chapters.summary: Maren's POV then Oscar's. The guard betrays them for restored memories of his lost family; Maren is captured and memory-wiped, forgetting Oscar entirely. Oscar reaches the throne room but hesitates—the unbinding rite demands the sigil-bearer's own memories as fuel. Emotional beat: devastating loss; the cost of power made flesh.

chapters.title: Eclipse of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. Under the eclipsed moon, Oscar begins the unbinding, feeding the sigil their forged temple life, their debts, their carefully built invisibility. The Vessel fights back with Aldric's own worst memories. Oscar anchors themselves with one truth it cannot counterfeit—and tears the crown's hold apart. Emotional beat: triumphant self-erasure becoming self-definition.

chapters.title: A Hand Unbound
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, resolution. Aldric wakes mortal and diminished, grateful and grieving; he offers Oscar anything, and Oscar asks only for Maren's memories returned—which return imperfectly, a beginning rather than a restoration. The valley's old protections are gone, but so are Oscar's chains. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope as Oscar walks the open road, author of their own record at last.
